definitions.E3:
Thanks—that’s the **Construction Management Bachelor of Technology**, an active degree-completion program offered in person at the Burnaby campus, full-time or part-time. Its curriculum covers construction controls, organization management, stakeholder engagement, management electives, Liberal Studies, and professional standards, including **CMGT 8700 – Industry Based Project Proposal** followed by a choice of final project.

To determine what you should take next, which courses have you completed?

[Construction Management program page](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/construction-management-bachelor-of-technology-full-time-part-time-8800btech/)
definitions.E2:
Thanks. Since you haven’t completed any program courses, I can’t verify a specific “next” course because the curriculum record does not provide a starting sequence or prerequisite details.

The first curriculum area includes **CMGT 7160 – Statistics for Construction Management**, **CMGT 7190 – Construction Planning and Controls**, **CMGT 7211 – Heavy Equipment in Construction**, and **CMGT 7400 – Project Planning for Quality & Risk Management**. Confirm your initial schedule with the Construction Management department before registering.

[Construction Management program page](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/construction-management-bachelor-of-technology-full-time-part-time-8800btech/)
definitions.E1:
No—not yet. Since you haven’t completed any program courses, you must first:

- Complete **CMGT 8700**
- Have at least **two years of related work experience**; qualifying admission experience counts
- Obtain department approval for your chosen final project: **CMGT 8800** or **CMGT 8810**

You choose **one** of those two final-project options.
